I edited only `django/contrib/admin/options.py` in `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()`.

Summary of the change: I corrected the logic that builds `relation_parts` so that a relational field (ForeignKey/OneToOneField) is never skipped merely because it happens to be the target field of the previous relation. Previously, for a lookup like `restaurant__place__country` where `Restaurant.place` is a `OneToOneField(Place, primary_key=True)`, the `place` segment was dropped because it appeared in `restaurant.path_infos[-1].target_fields` (Restaurant's pk is `place`). That produced the bogus lookup `restaurant__country`, which is not in `list_filter`, so `lookup_allowed()` returned False and raised `DisallowedModelAdminLookup`. The fix ensures relation segments are retained so the full `restaurant__place__country` path is matched against `list_filter`.

Verification: I ran the scoped public regression selection (`modeladmin`), which passed — 162 tests ran, returncode 0, OK. Note that public regression success does not guarantee host feature acceptance, which the host runs separately.

Caveat on process: during editing I had a couple of malformed intermediate edits (an accidental duplicated block and a joined line) which I corrected; the final file state is syntactically valid and the public regression suite passes. I was unable to make further refinements because the work-request budget was exhausted.
